title: Bristol Myers' Lupus Drug Sotyktu Shows Mixed Results in Late-Stage Trials

contentHtml:
Bengaluru: US drugmaker Bristol Myers Squibb said on Wednesday its oral drug Sotyktu met the main goal of a late-stage trial in people with systemic lupus erythematosus, but missed it in another.

In the successful trial, a significantly higher share of patients taking Sotyktu showed reduced lupus disease activity after 52 weeks compared with those receiving a placebo, the company said.

Systemic lupus erythematosus is a chronic autoimmune disease that can cause fatigue, pain, inflammation and damage to organs.The drug also improved several other measures, including treatment response, the ability of some participants to lower their steroid use and patient-reported fatigue.

However, in another similarly designed late-stage trial, Sotyktu did not meet its main goal.

Bristol Myers said the result was affected by a higher response among patients receiving placebo than in the first study.

The drug was generally well-tolerated in both trials, with safety results consistent with its use in psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis, Bristol Myers said. Sotyktu is approved in the US for adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis and active psoriatic arthritis.

The drug is also being evaluated in Sjogren's autoimmune disease, with results expected in 2027.

Source : Reuters
